import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Green's Open Problem 44

*References:*
- [Gr24] [Ben Green's 100 Open Problems](https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.44)
- [Er80] Erdős, Paul. "A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory."
  Annals of Discrete Mathematics 6 (1980): 89-115.
-/

namespace Green44

open scoped Nat

/--
Sieve $[N]$ by removing half the residue classes mod $p_i$, for primes
$2 \leqslant p_1 < p_2 < \dots < p_{1000} < N^{9/10}$. Does the remaining set have size at most
$\frac{1}{10} N$?

We interpret "half the residue classes" as $\lfloor p_i / 2 \rfloor$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem green_44 :
    answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ (N : ℕ) (p : Fin 1000 → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin 1000) → Finset (ZMod (p i))),
      let remaining := (Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun x => ∀ i, (x : ZMod (p i)) ∉ A i)
      (∀ i, (p i).Prime) →
      StrictMono p →
      (p 999) ^ 10 < N ^ 9 →
      (∀ i, (A i).card = (p i) / 2) →
      10 * remaining.card ≤ N := by
  sorry

/-- The answer is affirmative if the primes are all less than $N^{1/2}$, by the large sieve. [Gr24] -/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem green_44.variants.less_than_sqrt :
    ∀ (N : ℕ) (p : Fin 1000 → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin 1000) → Finset (ZMod (p i))),
      let remaining := (Finset.Icc 1 N).filter (fun x => ∀ i, (x : ZMod (p i)) ∉ A i)
      (∀ i, (p i).Prime) →
      StrictMono p →
      (p 999) ^ 2 < N →
      (∀ i, (A i).card = (p i) / 2) →
      10 * remaining.card ≤ N := by
  sorry

end Green44

findings.description: The unqualified `∀ (N : ℕ)` makes the right-hand side provably false by an elementary finite-N construction. Take N = 100000 and any 1000 of the 1078 primes in [20003,31000]. Their maximum satisfies p^10 < N^9. For each prime, remove the residues (p+1)/2, …, p−1: exactly floor(p/2) classes. All integers 1,…,10001 survive, so 10 * remaining.card ≥ 100010 > N. I verified the negation of the exact universal RHS in Lean. Thus this reading trivializes the purported open question; a sufficiently-large-N interpretation appears intended. However, Green's wording itself does not explicitly include that qualification, so this is flagged as a modelling ambiguity rather than a definitive mistranscription.
findings.source_evidence: Green, 100 Open Problems, p. 22, Problem 44 (https://people.maths.ox.ac.uk/greenbj/papers/open-problems.pdf#problem.44), asks: “Sieve [N] by removing half the residue classes mod p_i, for primes 2 ≤ p_1 < … < p_1000 < N^{9/10}. Does the remaining set have size at most (1/10)N?” Its comments cite Erdős, A survey of problems in combinatorial number theory, §6, Problem 3, p. 107 (https://www.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1980-03.pdf). Erdős's formulation asks for an unspecified k = k₀(ε,η), and describes the general case as intractable. Neither this reference nor Green's terse wording resolves the intended finite-N scope of the fixed-1000 formulation.
findings.suggested_fix: Clarify the intended N-scope. To capture the open large-N reading, replace the outer universal quantifier by `answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ᶠ (N : ℕ) in Filter.atTop, ∀ (p : Fin 1000 → ℕ) (A : (i : Fin 1000) → Finset (ZMod (p i))), ...`, leaving the remaining hypotheses and conclusion unchanged. Explain the implicit largeness qualification in the docstring. The cutoff must be uniform in p and A; merely adding N > 0 does not fix the counterexample.

reformulations.difference: The numerical bounds use natural-number inequalities `p 999 ^ 10 < N ^ 9` and `10 * remaining.card ≤ N`, rather than real powers and the fraction N/10. This observation concerns only the numerical encoding, independently of the N-scope issue.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For nonnegative natural p and N, raising to the tenth power gives p < N^(9/10) iff p^10 < N^9. Multiplication by the positive real number 10 gives |remaining| ≤ N/10 iff 10|remaining| ≤ N. Also, StrictMono p makes p 999 the largest prime, so bounding it bounds every p i. These component equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

reformulations.difference: The source's condition that every prime is less than N^(1/2) is expressed as `p 999 ^ 2 < N`; its fractional cardinality bound is also cleared of denominators.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For natural p and N, p² < N iff (p : ℝ) < sqrt(N). StrictMono makes index 999 the maximum of the 1000-element family, and clearing the positive denominator 10 preserves the cardinality inequality exactly. These equivalences were proved in /workspace/review/scratch.lean.

could_not_verify: Green44.green_44 — The source does not explicitly settle whether “for sufficiently large N” is implicit in the fixed-1000 question. The literal all-N version has been rigorously refuted, but deciding whether its formalization is faithful requires resolving this source-interpretation ambiguity.
review.notes: All three verification files compiled successfully: /workspace/review/scratch.lean, nonvacuity.lean, and counterexample.lean. The counterexample proves the negation of the current universal RHS without using either Green44 theorem or sorry; native_decide is used only to certify that the finite prime pool contains at least 1000 primes. Boundary evaluations confirmed the interval, casts, and floor-division semantics, and a separate construction established joint satisfiability of the hypotheses. No defect was found in the square-root variant: the usual large-sieve estimate gives an upper bound below 2N/501, comfortably stronger than N/10. Green's current source still lists Problem 44 as open and its square-root case as affirmative; the finite-N issue is not being reported as a source-recorded status change. The target file was not modified.
